It receives cadence obligations, classifies new tests through the independent matcher when necessary, selects tests, preserves legacy cadence metadata contracts, and proves cadence coverage before execution.

governingDocuments.governingDocuments/agent-progress-policy: Mandatory attended-agent progress continuity, America/New_York timestamping, completion/interruption check-ins, and continue-until-done behavior.

sessionPolicy.recheckGoverningDocuments: Re-read every file listed in governingDocuments at the start of every session and again any time more than 10 minutes have passed since lastActionAt, even if it is the same agent continuing the same conversation.

agentCommunicationPolicy.timestampRule: Every attended progress, completion, and interruption check-in begins with YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EDT when daylight-saving time is active or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EST otherwise; never use ambiguous ET or UTC-only user updates.
agentCommunicationPolicy.progressRule: For non-trivial attended work, send an initial update and continue user-visible updates at least every 60 seconds, normally also after every 2-3 substantive tool/action calls when sooner, with concrete completed/current/blocker state.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionTimeRule: When work duration is not mechanically knowable, provide a clearly labeled best-effort estimated completion timestamp in America/New_York time when the owner requests one; never present an estimate as guaranteed or as an externally fixed completion time.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionCheckInRule: As soon as attended work is actually complete, automatically send a timestamped completion check-in in the same session with concrete result, verification, and relevant commit/run identifiers.
agentCommunicationPolicy.interruptionCheckInRule: If hard usage/tool/session limits, unavailable required capability, safety, or owner-governance boundaries stop work, immediately send a timestamped interruption check-in stating completed work, exact stop reason, and remaining work; update repository handoff first when write capability remains.
agentCommunicationPolicy.continueUntilDoneRule: For safe in-scope authorized work, do not voluntarily stop, defer, or hand work back while executable work remains. Continue through implementation, correction, and required verification until complete or until a hard usage/tool/session limit or higher-priority platform, safety, or owner-governance boundary prevents further execution.

syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.description: The CRUCIBLE TEST REQUEST synthetic commit-message transport exists only because the current ChatGPT/GitHub integration cannot directly create the required Orchestrator invocation. It is a workaround, not the intended architecture.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.replacementRequirement: Replace and remove this workaround as soon as a supported direct integration or direct connection exists that can pass the user's natural-language test request to the Orchestrator without manufacturing a repository commit.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.targetArchitecture: User test request -> supported direct integration/connection -> Orchestrator -> Orchestrator alone selects and runs tests -> results.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.standingOwnerAuthorization: The owner explicitly authorizes this specific replacement as soon as the supported direct integration/connection capability exists; no additional approval is required solely for that replacement.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.scopeBoundary: This authorization does not authorize unrelated repository changes or promotion to main/release.

testCadencePolicy.systemArchitecture: Orchestrator, Cadence, closest-feature classification, and reconciliation operate as one governed testing system while remaining independent checks-and-balances authorities; they must not be collapsed into one selector.
testCadencePolicy.cadenceAuthority: Cadence decides only when a category is due. It produces a due-category obligation and never selects files, classifies new tests, interprets natural-language scope, or executes tests.
testCadencePolicy.classifierAuthority: The independent closest-feature classifier is fallback-only for newly discovered tests absent from the explicit category map. It compares the new test with known feature/test evidence and returns a category only for a unique closest match. It cannot choose run scope, set frequency, or execute tests.
testCadencePolicy.classificationAmbiguityRule: Isolate ambiguity, continue safe tests, never fake complete coverage. If a newly discovered test remains unresolved after independent closest-feature classification, quarantine that test from guessed execution and report its unresolved classification while continuing all other safely classified tests selected by the Orchestrator. Do not globally abort unrelated safe tests solely because one new test is unresolved. If the unresolved test is required to satisfy an explicit owner request or cadence obligation, mark that requested coverage incomplete and do not report the obligation or suite as fully passing until the ambiguity is resolved and the required test is executed.
testCadencePolicy.explicitMappingRule: Existing explicit category mappings are authoritative and are never overridden by the closest-feature classifier.
testCadencePolicy.orchestratorAuthority: The Orchestrator alone selects categories/subcategories/test files and execution scope from explicit requests, change impact, dependencies, cadence obligations, and validated classifications.
testCadencePolicy.balanceRule: For cadence-triggered work, Cadence declares categories due; the Orchestrator independently resolves them into concrete tests; reconciliation rejects a claim of complete cadence coverage if any due category is omitted. Neither authority silently overrides the other.
testCadencePolicy.explicitRequestRule: A specific owner test request is interpreted and run immediately by the Orchestrator. Cadence and classification cannot delay, randomize, narrow, or replace an explicit request; unresolved classification may make coverage incomplete but must not suppress unrelated safe testing.
testCadencePolicy.standingTestExpansionRule: New standing test cases may be added inside an already explicitly categorized test file when they belong to that same category. They inherit that file's governed category and the category's cadence without creating a redundant test-file mapping. New standalone .test.js files still require explicit classification or independent closest-feature fallback.
testCadencePolicy.codeCriticalityRule: Code is due on every push and pull request. The Orchestrator independently selects the complete Code category required to satisfy that cadence obligation.
testCadencePolicy.scheduledCumulativeRule: Cadence obligations are cumulative: daily requires Code and Security; twice-weekly requires Code, Security, and Utility; weekly/monthly require all four categories.
testCadencePolicy.twiceWeeklySchedule: Utility is due Tuesdays and Fridays; scheduled-diagnostics transports only the cadence window.
